newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa Chamber of Mines urges more to join ranks.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa Chamber of Mines urges more to join ranks.

text.p: South Africa's Chamber of Mines on Tuesday urged more mining companies to join its ranks, saying the industry needed a fully representative body with which to lobby government and labour.

Speaking at the Chamber's 106th annual general meeting, outgoing president At du Plessis said: "Several major mining companies which have previously not been full members of the Chamber have joined its ranks. Indications are that other companies will follow in due course.
"A more representative Chamber of Mines is essential if the industry is to secure the best possible regulatory environment for mining activity," he said.
The Chamber is an employer body which represents coal and gold mines. Large mining houses such as Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd and Gencor Ltd are members.
Du Plessis said that the Chamber's fundamental focus was being shifted to the lobbying of government, labour and "other significant protagonists in the national public policy arena".
Against this background, he said that the Chamber had embarked on a vigorous drive to attract more members to enable it to be fully representative of the entire mining industry.
A more representative Chamber would ensure that mining played its full role in the national economy for years to come, du Plessis added.
